- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day forecast horizon, especially for the first 5–7 days.
- Model tends to overreact to recent price spikes, overshooting the true value by 2–5% in the immediate aftermath.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: after a sharp spike, it incorrectly assumes prices will fall too quickly, underestimating the sustained level.
- Forecast accuracy improves as the horizon extends beyond day 10–15, suggesting model struggles with short-term dynamics.
- Model often fails to capture the “rebound” phase after a sharp decline — it underestimates the recovery, leading to persistent underprediction.
- Model shows a lag in responding to recent price changes — it takes 3–5 days to adjust its forecast after a new high or low is observed.
- Model tends to overestimate volatility in the first 5 days, leading to overly conservative (low) forecasts that later rebound.
- Model underestimates the true mean of the price series, especially in the first 10 days, suggesting a persistent downward bias in the early forecast window.
